title: Trump Promotes Hydroxychloroquine for COVID-19; FDA Revokes Stockpile EUA
description_medium: In March 2020, Donald Trump promoted hydroxychloroquine as a possible COVID-19 treatment, calling it a “game changer” and asking, “What do you have to lose?” On June 15, the FDA revoked emergency authorization for stockpiled chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine for certain hospitalized patients, citing little likelihood of benefit and serious cardiac risks.
description_long: Donald Trump publicly promoted hydroxychloroquine as a possible treatment for COVID-19 in spring 2020, describing it as a “game changer” and asking what patients had to lose. At the time, the FDA had authorized use of donated chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine from the Strategic National Stockpile for certain hospitalized patients when clinical-trial participation was unavailable or infeasible. On June 15, 2020, the agency revoked that emergency authorization after reviewing new evidence. The FDA said the drugs were unlikely to be effective for the authorized uses and that potential benefits no longer outweighed known and potential risks, including serious cardiac events. A large randomized trial in hospitalized patients had found no benefit on mortality or speed of recovery. Hydroxychloroquine remains approved for malaria and certain autoimmune conditions, but the COVID-19 emergency authorization was limited to the specified hospitalized-patient setting.

corrected_wording.original_title: Hydroxychloroquine Death Push - Deadly Drug Promotion
corrected_wording.corrected_title: Trump Promotes Hydroxychloroquine for COVID-19; FDA Revokes Stockpile EUA
corrected_wording.reason: The evidence supports Trump’s promotion and the FDA’s risk-based revocation, but not a causal death toll or demonstrated medication shortage.

source_access_notes: FDA’s June 15, 2020 notice supplies the authorization scope and reasons for revocation; the statements attributed to Trump are documented in the supplied timeline context.
blockers: The available sources document Trump’s promotion and the FDA’s revocation but do not substantiate the original title’s implied causal death toll or medication shortages.
rationale: Corrects the title to the documented promotion and FDA regulatory decision; causal claims about deaths or shortages remain unsupported, so the long description is intentionally partial.

title: Trump Names Steven Cheung Communications Director and Karoline Leavitt Press Secretary
description_medium: On November 15, 2024, president-elect Donald Trump named Steven Cheung, his campaign communications director, to lead the incoming White House communications office and selected campaign spokesperson Karoline Leavitt as press secretary. Both appointments carried campaign aides into senior public-facing administration roles and signaled continuity in Trump’s communications team.
description_long: President-elect Donald Trump announced on November 15, 2024, that Steven Cheung would serve as White House communications director and Karoline Leavitt as press secretary. Cheung had led communications for Trump’s 2024 campaign and served as director of strategic response during Trump’s first term. Leavitt had been the campaign’s press secretary and was selected to become the administration’s principal public spokesperson. The two jobs are distinct: the communications director coordinates the president’s broader messaging operation, while the press secretary answers questions and represents the White House in briefings. The selections placed campaign aides in central roles in the incoming administration’s relationship with the news media. Trump also announced Sergio Gor as director of the Presidential Personnel Office in the same transition announcement. These were appointments announced before inauguration, not actions by officials already exercising the duties of those offices. At 27, Leavitt was set to become the youngest White House press secretary.

corrected_wording.original_title: Trump names bomb thrower Steven Cheung as communications director
corrected_wording.corrected_title: Trump Names Steven Cheung Communications Director and Karoline Leavitt Press Secretary
corrected_wording.reason: “Bomb thrower” is editorial characterization; the documented event is the announcement of two White House communications appointments.

source_access_notes: Reuters reported the transition announcement and the White House later listed the appointments in its official staffing announcement.
rationale: Describes the transition appointments and their roles while replacing the editorial label with relevant context about Leavitt’s appointment.
